content: The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are taking other medications that elevate serotonin levels. Examples of such substances include illicit drugs like MDMA (commonly known as ecstasy), herbal supplements such as St. John’s Wort, and certain antidepressants, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) like fluoxetine or paroxetine, and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) like duloxetine or venlafaxine. Always inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the medications and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). If the symptoms are less severe, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as an electrocardiogram (EKG), to monitor your condition and ensure the medication is working safely. Be sure to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. This medication is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer treatments such as chemotherapy or radiation therapy, as well as medications used to induce anesthesia before surgery. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully when using this medication. To use the oral soluble film, read the patient information leaflet and instructions provided by your pharmacist. With dry hands, open the protective foil pouch just before use. Place one film on top of your tongue and allow it to dissolve completely, which usually takes 4 to 20 seconds. Swallow the dissolved medication with saliva or liquid. If your dose requires more than one film, allow each film to dissolve completely before taking the next one. To prevent nausea from chemotherapy, take this medication as directed by your doctor, typically 30 minutes before treatment begins. For nausea prevention from radiation therapy, take it 1 to 2 hours before the start of treatment. Ondansetron may be taken up to three times a day for 1 to 2 days after each chemotherapy or radiation session. Take it regularly if prescribed on a schedule to maximize its benefits. Dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and, for children, their age and weight. Common side effects include headache, lightheadedness, dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, or constipation. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may increase serotonin levels and lead to a serious condition called serotonin syndrome or toxicity. The risk is higher if you are taking other drugs that increase serotonin levels. Notify your doctor or pharmacist of all the medications you are taking to avoid this risk. Ondansetron may rarely cause a serious allergic reaction. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking ondansetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Ondansetron may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using certain medications (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Examples of drugs that may interact with ondansetron include MDMA, St. John’s Wort, SSRIs, and SNRIs.
